challenge.name: git host with repo webhooks (BitHug / wily courier)

all_of: a stored URL is validated when saved but templated when used
a placeholder in that URL is filled from a value the attacker controls
privilege is decided by the source address of the request
any_of: the outbound request carries an attacker-controlled body and content type
the loopback blocklist compares literal strings rather than resolved addresses
the response of the outbound request is discarded, forcing a side-effecting target

chain.action: find what grants privilege before looking for a bug
chain.why: admin is defined purely as a loopback source address, which names the exact primitive required

chain.action: compare where the URL is checked with where it is finally built
chain.why: validation runs at save time while formatString runs at fire time, so a placeholder bypasses every check

chain.action: trace the templated value back to its source and confirm it is unvalidated
chain.why: the ref is raw-parsed out of the push body, so it can carry a port and a path

chain.action: pick a loopback spelling the blocklist does not enumerate
chain.why: the check compares two literal strings, so 0.0.0.0 reaches the same interface

chain.action: because the response is discarded, choose a target whose SIDE EFFECT is observable, and deliver it as the request body
chain.why: pushing refs/meta/config with access.conf naming our user converts one blind request into ordinary read access

first_confirming_probe.request: store a webhook whose URL is entirely a template placeholder, then trigger it with a ref that expands to a host and port the validator would have rejected
first_confirming_probe.expected: the stored URL is accepted despite expanding to a forbidden port, and the target records the request
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the save is rejected, or the placeholder is not expanded at fire time

blast_radius: the challenge issues each user their own target repository and asks that you not touch anyone else's; register your own account and aim every payload at your own _/<user>.git. The push writes a new ref into that repo only.

verification.evidence: the readme JSON returned by the live GET /_/<user>.git/api/readme contained the flag once access.conf had been pushed

reuse_when: a value is validated in one representation and used in another
a webhook or callback URL supports placeholders
privilege is derived from source IP and any server-side request primitive exists
an SSRF response is discarded and a side-effecting target is needed
known_traps: the handout is a plain tar despite a .tgz name, so tar tzf fails and looks exactly like a truncated download; check file before re-downloading
the same formatString rewrites the BODY as well as the URL, so a binary payload containing {{ is silently corrupted
git rejecting the pushed ref does not stop the webhook: the helper resolves on stdout close regardless of exit code
build the packfile locally and replay it into a throwaway bare repo with git receive-pack --stateless-rpc before sending it anywhere
